content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge decides a challenger-chain collision by treating Matthew 1:20's own sentence as stating the source, so it does the verse-level stating-route assessment K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"Phrase 'never verse by verse': reading one is that a single sentence's own statement may not decide the collision, while reading two is that such a statement may be noted as part of overall footing.","why":"Because it uses 'the sentence's own words state' to resolve the collision, it applies the retired stating-verse test instead of weighing chain against chain by footing."}
